            # audit 2026-07-24). Constant across models in the same row, so
            # ΔAIC is unchanged — but absolute AIC/BIC are now honest.
            'n_params_total': int(len(model.free_parameters)),
            'params': params,
            'minos_ok': (minos_table is not None),
            'epk_curve': epk_curve,
            'width_hm': width_hm,
        }
    except Exception as exc:
        return {'status': 'FAIL', 'reason': str(exc)[:120],
                'neg2logL': float('nan'), 'n_params': spec['n_params'],
                'params': {}, 'minos_ok': False}


def model_columns(spec, result, n_data):
    """Flatten a fit result into ECSV columns prefixed with spec['prefix']."""
    p = spec['prefix']
    out = {f'{p}_STATUS': result.get('status', 'NA'),
           f'{p}_N2LL':   result.get('neg2logL', float('nan')),
           f'{p}_MINOS_OK': bool(result.get('minos_ok', False)),
           # honest labels (Codex 3ML audit): MINOS_OK only means get_errors
           # returned a table (per-side validity flags are not propagated by
           # threeML); the symmetric 'error' column is covariance-MC equal-tail,
           # NOT a direct Hessian sigma. AIC here is RAW AIC (-2logL + 2k),
           # not threeML's AICc.
           f'{p}_ERROR_METHOD': ('MINOS' if result.get('minos_ok', False)
                                 else 'COVARIANCE_MC'),
           f'{p}_VALID': bool(result.get('physical', False))}
    if result.get('status') == 'OK':
        n2ll = result['neg2logL']
        # k = true free-parameter count incl. EAC/LAT nuisances when available
        nk = result.get('n_params_total') or result['n_params']
        out[f'{p}_AIC'] = n2ll + 2 * nk
        out[f'{p}_BIC'] = n2ll + nk * np.log(max(n_data, 1))
    else:
        out[f'{p}_AIC'] = float('nan')
        out[f'{p}_BIC'] = float('nan')
    # peak-shape statistics from the fitted curve (NaN when peak not interior)
    out[f'{p}_EPK_CURVE'] = result.get('epk_curve', float('nan'))
    out[f'{p}_WIDTH_HM'] = result.get('width_hm', float('nan'))
    for col_suffix, short in spec['pmap'].items():
        d = result.get('params', {}).get(short)
        if d is None:
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}']         = float('nan')
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_ERR']     = float('nan')
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_NEG_ERR'] = float('nan')
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_POS_ERR'] = float('nan')
        else:
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}']         = d['val']
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_ERR']     = d['err']
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_NEG_ERR'] = d['neg']
            out[f'{p}_{col_suffix}_POS_ERR'] = d['pos']
                 'dsbpl_xp': 1000.0, 'dsbpl_beta': -2.6, 'dsbpl_K': 1.0}]
            if all(v is not None and np.isfinite(v) for v in (a_s, br_s, b_s, k_s)):
                for frac in (0.2, 0.4, 0.6):             # trial low break BELOW the SBPL break
                    xb_try = float(np.clip(br_s * frac, 10.0, 4900.0))
                    if xb_try < br_s:
                        DSBPL_RESTART_SEEDS.append({
                            'dsbpl_alpha1': a_s, 'dsbpl_xb': xb_try,
                            'dsbpl_alpha2': 0.5 * (a_s + b_s), 'dsbpl_xp': br_s,
                            'dsbpl_beta': b_s, 'dsbpl_K': k_s})
            best_d = dsbpl_res
            for extra in DSBPL_RESTART_SEEDS:
                s = extra if extra == {} else {**seed_in, **extra}
                alt = fit_one_model(dl, dsbpl_spec, seed=s)
                alt['physical'] = _fit_is_physical(dsbpl_spec, alt)
                if _keep_best(alt, best_d):        # validity-preferring (L8)
                    best_d = alt
            if best_d is not dsbpl_res:
                print(f'    [DSBPL multistart] n2logL '
                      f'{dsbpl_res.get("neg2logL", float("nan")):.1f} -> {best_d["neg2logL"]:.1f}')
                per_spec[idxs['DSBPL']] = (dsbpl_spec, best_d)
                flat.update(model_columns(dsbpl_spec, best_d, n_data))
                seed_out.update(capture_seed(dsbpl_spec, best_d))

    # Cutoff-xc multi-start. The multiplicative high-E cutoff (BandxCut, SBPLxCut)
    # is degenerate with the continuum shape: in a free joint fit the single-shot
    # minuit solution can settle at a spurious xc->floor minimum (exp(-E/xc) acting
    # as a low-band curvature knob with a hardened continuum) that BEATS the
    # no-cutoff parent -- so the generic nested-parent pass below (which fires only
    # when the child is WORSE than a parent) never re-explores it. The xc floor is
    # now 100 MeV (LAT band, see _setup_cutoff_mult); this pass additionally seeds
    # xc ACROSS the band and keeps the lowest n2logL, so the fit lands on the
    # genuine high-energy cutoff the LAT term demands (verified: GRB 160625B coarse
    # bins, LAT term alone prefers xc~200-400 MeV, TS~90; per-plugin decomposition
    # 2026-07-22). Keep-best -> never worsens a fit.
    CUT_RESTART_SEEDS = [{},                          # default seed (xc=500 MeV)
                         {'cut_xc': 1.5e5},           # 150 MeV
                         {'cut_xc': 3.0e5},           # 300 MeV
                         {'cut_xc': 7.0e5},           # 700 MeV
                         {'cut_xc': 2.0e6}]           # 2 GeV
    idxs = {s['name']: i for i, (s, _) in enumerate(per_spec)}
    for child_name in ('BandxCut', 'SBPLxCut'):
        if child_name not in idxs:
            continue
        child_spec, child_res = per_spec[idxs[child_name]]
        best_c = child_res
        for extra in CUT_RESTART_SEEDS:
            s = extra if extra == {} else {**seed_in, **extra}
            alt = fit_one_model(dl, child_spec, seed=s)
            alt['physical'] = _fit_is_physical(child_spec, alt)
            if _keep_best(alt, best_c):            # validity-preferring (L8)
                best_c = alt
        if best_c is not child_res:
            print(f'    [cutoff multistart] {child_name} n2logL '
                  f'{child_res.get("neg2logL", float("nan")):.1f} '
                  f'-> {best_c["neg2logL"]:.1f}')
            per_spec[idxs[child_name]] = (child_spec, best_c)
            flat.update(model_columns(child_spec, best_c, n_data))
            seed_out.update(capture_seed(child_spec, best_c))

    # Generic NESTED-PARENT multistart (Codex ultra audit CRITICAL #4): every
    # composite whose n2logL is WORSE than a nested parent's is at a local
    # minimum (impossible at the true optimum — the parent solution + a null
    # extra component reproduces the parent's likelihood). Re-fit such children
    # seeded from each FITTED parent (capture_seed gives exactly the child's
    # shared seed keys), plus hot-kT variants for +BB children. Keep-best;
    # 2-component entries run before 3-component so children seed from FINAL
    # parents. The audit measured 8-12/19-25 regressed fits per 3-component
    # model with N2LL excesses up to ~7000 before this.
    idxs = {s['name']: i for i, (s, _) in enumerate(per_spec)}
    for child_name, parent_names in NESTED_PARENTS:
        if child_name not in idxs:
            continue
        child_spec, child_res = per_spec[idxs[child_name]]
        parents = [(per_spec[idxs[p]][0], per_spec[idxs[p]][1])
                   for p in parent_names if p in idxs]
        p_ok = [(ps, pr) for ps, pr in parents
                if pr.get('status') == 'OK' and np.isfinite(pr.get('neg2logL', np.nan))]
        if not p_ok:
            continue
        parent_best = min(pr['neg2logL'] for _, pr in p_ok)
        c_ok = (child_res.get('status') == 'OK'
                and np.isfinite(child_res.get('neg2logL', np.nan)))
        if c_ok and child_res['neg2logL'] <= parent_best + 1e-3:
            continue                     # already at/below every parent
        best = child_res
        for pspec, pres in p_ok:
            base = {**seed_in, **capture_seed(pspec, pres)}
            trials = [base]
            if 'KT' in child_spec.get('pmap', {}):
                trials += [{**base, 'bb_kT': 30.0, 'bb_K': 1e-3},
                           {**base, 'bb_kT': 80.0, 'bb_K': 1e-3}]
            for s in trials:
                alt = fit_one_model(dl, child_spec, seed=s)
                alt['physical'] = _fit_is_physical(child_spec, alt)
                if (alt.get('status') == 'OK' and np.isfinite(alt['neg2logL'])
                        and (best.get('status') != 'OK'
                             or not np.isfinite(best.get('neg2logL', np.nan))
                             or alt['neg2logL'] < best['neg2logL'] - 1e-3)):
                    best = alt
        if best is not child_res:
            print(f'    [nested multistart] {child_name} n2logL '
                  f'{child_res.get("neg2logL", float("nan")):.1f} '
                  f'-> {best["neg2logL"]:.1f} (parent best {parent_best:.1f})')
            per_spec[idxs[child_name]] = (child_spec, best)
            flat.update(model_columns(child_spec, best, n_data))
            seed_out.update(capture_seed(child_spec, best))

    # L9 BOUND_CAPPED diagnosis (bn110721200 blk0): when >=2 peaked models rail
    # their peak parameter at the SAME upper bound, the bin is bound-capped —
    # a false INCONCLUSIVE where the validity gate silently promotes the next
    # family. Stamp it (and shout) instead of letting that happen quietly.
    _peak_cols = ('EP', 'EBREAK', 'XP')
    _rail_at = {}
    for sp_, r_ in per_spec:
        if r_.get('status') != 'OK':
            continue
        pb_ = PARAM_BOUNDS.get(sp_['prefix'], {})
        for col_ in _peak_cols:
            if col_ not in pb_:
                continue
            short_ = sp_['pmap'].get(col_)
            d_ = r_.get('params', {}).get(short_) if short_ else None
            if d_ is None or not np.isfinite(d_.get('val', np.nan)):
                continue
            hi_ = pb_[col_][1]
            if d_['val'] >= 0.98 * hi_:
                _rail_at.setdefault(hi_, []).append(sp_['name'])
    _bc = [f"{hi_:g}:{'+'.join(sorted(set(nm_)))}"
           for hi_, nm_ in _rail_at.items() if len(set(nm_)) >= 2]
    flat['BOUND_CAPPED'] = ';'.join(_bc)
    if _bc:
        print(f'    !! BOUND_CAPPED {_bc} — peaked models rail at a shared '
              f'bound; widen and refit, do not trust the surviving family')

    # SHARPNESS_CAPPED (bn130518580 blk6, 2026-08-08 four-channel audit): a
    # one-break model whose free break SHARPNESS rails at its bound (SBPLfree
    # break_scale=2.0, DSBPLfree n1/n2=10) is gated VALID=False and silently
    # vanishes from the margin's reference set — inflating "extra structure"
    # margins computed vs the best VALID one-break (blk6: 18.66 apparent vs
    # <=4.75 admitting the capped fit as a lower limit). The EP/EBREAK/XP
    # inspector above never fires on sharpness. Stamp it and shout: margins
    # in a stamped block exclude a deeper capped one-break minimum.
    _sharp_cols = ('SCALE', 'N1', 'N2')
    _sc = []
    for sp_, r_ in per_spec:
        if r_.get('status') != 'OK':
            continue
        pb_ = PARAM_BOUNDS.get(sp_['prefix'], {})
        for col_ in _sharp_cols:
            if col_ not in pb_:
                continue
            short_ = sp_['pmap'].get(col_)
            d_ = r_.get('params', {}).get(short_) if short_ else None
            if d_ is None or not np.isfinite(d_.get('val', np.nan)):
                continue
            lo_, hi_ = pb_[col_]
            span_ = hi_ - lo_
            if (d_['val'] - lo_) < 0.02 * span_ or (hi_ - d_['val']) < 0.02 * span_:
                _sc.append(f"{sp_['name']}:{col_}@{d_['val']:g}")
    flat['SHARPNESS_CAPPED'] = ';'.join(_sc)
    if _sc:
        print(f'    !! SHARPNESS_CAPPED {_sc} — a free break-sharpness railed; '
              f'margins vs the best VALID one-break exclude a deeper capped '
              f'minimum and are UPPER LIMITS, not measurements')

    flat.update(select_best(per_spec, n_data))
    flat['_n_data'] = n_data
    return flat, seed_out

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
model_registry.py -- THE single source of truth for the spectral-model census
(Codex ultra audit CRITICAL #5/#6: scripts/10, 31 and the ad-hoc censuses each
had their own model lists / parent maps / selection rules, and scripts/31
silently converted every new-family winner to INCONCLUSIVE).

Defines, once:
  - the full 24-model prefix registry with display names and families;
  - the NESTED-PARENT map (a composite is admissible only if it beats EVERY
    nested parent by DAIC_GATE -- same map scripts/10's multistart uses);
  - the LOCKED selection doctrine (2026-06 framework):
      * a fit survives if VALID (physical, non-railed), STATUS OK, finite AIC,
        and (if composite) beats every parent by >= DAIC_GATE;
      * the block's WINNER is the min-AIC survivor ONLY when it beats the
        runner-up survivor by >= DAIC_GATE (top-two doctrine);
      * otherwise the block is INCONCLUSIVE (never silently assigned).

Import from the scripts dir (importlib, as the scripts do for each other) or
run:  python scripts/model_registry.py <spectral_fits.ecsv...>  for a census.
"""
import numpy as np

DAIC_GATE = 10.0          # locked ΔAIC≥10 doctrine (≡ LRT≥14 for 2 params)

# prefix -> (display name, family)
MODELS = {
    'BAND':      ('Band',        'single'),
    'CPL':       ('CPL',         'single'),
    'SBPL':      ('SBPL',        'single'),
    'DSBPL':     ('2SBPL',       'twobreak'),
    'SBPLF':     ('SBPLfree',    'single'),
    'DSBPLF':    ('2SBPLfree',   'twobreak'),
    'BANDBB':    ('Band+BB',     'thermal'),
    'CPLBB':     ('CPL+BB',      'thermal'),
    'SBPLBB':    ('SBPL+BB',     'thermal'),
    'BANDPL':    ('Band+PL',     'highe'),
    'BANDCPL':   ('Band+CPL',    'highe'),
    'CPLPL':     ('CPL+PL',      'highe'),
    'CPLCPL':    ('CPL+CPL',     'highe'),
    'SBPLPL':    ('SBPL+PL',     'highe'),
    'SBPLCPL':   ('SBPL+CPL',    'highe'),
    'BANDRCPL':  ('BandR+CPL',   'highe'),
    'BANDCUT':   ('BandxCut',    'cutoff'),
    'SBPLCUT':   ('SBPLxCut',    'cutoff'),
    'BANDBBPL':  ('Band+BB+PL',  'threecomp'),
    'BANDBBCPL': ('Band+BB+CPL', 'threecomp'),
    'CPLBBPL':   ('CPL+BB+PL',   'threecomp'),
    'CPLBBCPL':  ('CPL+BB+CPL',  'threecomp'),
    'SBPLBBPL':  ('SBPL+BB+PL',  'threecomp'),
    'SBPLBBCPL': ('SBPL+BB+CPL', 'threecomp'),
}

# composite prefix -> nested-parent prefixes (must beat EVERY parent by the gate)
PARENTS = {
    'BANDBB': ['BAND'], 'CPLBB': ['CPL'], 'SBPLBB': ['SBPL'],
    'BANDPL': ['BAND'], 'BANDCPL': ['BAND'],
    'CPLPL': ['CPL'], 'CPLCPL': ['CPL'],
    'SBPLPL': ['SBPL'], 'SBPLCPL': ['SBPL'],
    'BANDCUT': ['BAND'], 'SBPLCUT': ['SBPL'],
    'BANDRCPL': ['BAND'],
    'DSBPL': ['SBPL'], 'DSBPLF': ['SBPL'],
    'BANDBBPL': ['BANDBB', 'BANDPL'],
    'BANDBBCPL': ['BANDBB', 'BANDCPL'],
    'CPLBBPL': ['CPLBB', 'CPLPL'],
    'CPLBBCPL': ['CPLBB', 'CPLCPL'],
    'SBPLBBPL': ['SBPLBB', 'SBPLPL'],
    'SBPLBBCPL': ['SBPLBB', 'SBPLCPL'],
}

# scripts/10 NESTED_PARENTS equivalence (by display name) -- derived, one truth
NESTED_PARENTS_BY_NAME = [
    (MODELS[c][0], [MODELS[p][0] for p in ps]) for c, ps in PARENTS.items()
    if c not in ('DSBPL', 'DSBPLF')     # DSBPL has its own dedicated multistart
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DEGENERACY CLASSES (Vikas 2026-07-18): some model pairs are intrinsically
# degenerate over the fitted band — they re-adjust parameters to mimic each
# other, so a top-two AIC gap between them is structurally impossible and must
# NOT be read as "the data are ambiguous about the SHAPE". Declared a priori:
#   * 'extra_lowE_curvature': a thermal bump on a single-break continuum bends
#     nu-F-nu almost exactly like a second power-law break over the GBM band
#     (the draft's founding BB+SBPL <-> 2SBPL proxy). Distinguishing them needs
#     prompt LOW-energy coverage (XRT/optical) we do not have.
# The HIGH-E composites are deliberately NOT merged: above the peak an extra
# PL, a cutoff, and a saddle genuinely differ, and LLE/LAT sit there — that is
# exactly the regime where our band BREAKS the degeneracy.
# Census reports THREE levels: exact model (strict top-two), degeneracy class
# (top-two ACROSS classes; internal degeneracy reported separately), family.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEGENERACY_CLASSES = {
    'extra_lowE_curvature': {'DSBPL', 'DSBPLF', 'BANDBB', 'CPLBB', 'SBPLBB'},
}


def class_of(prefix):
    """Degeneracy-class label for a prefix (its own name when not merged)."""
    for cname, members in DEGENERACY_CLASSES.items():
        if prefix in members:
            return cname
    return prefix


def _val(row, col):
    try:
        return float(row[col])
    except Exception:
        return float('nan')


def is_valid(row, prefix, cols):
    """VALID (physical) + STATUS OK + finite AIC for this prefix in this row."""
    vc, sc, ac = f'{prefix}_VALID', f'{prefix}_STATUS', f'{prefix}_AIC'
    if ac not in cols:
        return False
    okv = (vc not in cols) or str(row[vc]) in ('True', '1', '1.0')
    oks = (sc not in cols) or str(row[sc]).lower() in ('ok', 'converged',
                                                       'success', 'true')
    return okv and oks and np.isfinite(_val(row, ac))


def survivors(row, cols, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """{prefix: AIC} of chain-gated, valid, finite fits in this row."""
    out = {}
    for p in MODELS:
        if not is_valid(row, p, cols):
            continue
        aic = _val(row, f'{p}_AIC')
        ok = True
        for par in PARENTS.get(p, []):
            if not is_valid(row, par, cols) or (_val(row, f'{par}_AIC') - aic) < daic:
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            out[p] = aic
    return out

def gated_winner(row, cols, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """(winner_prefix | 'INCONCLUSIVE', top2_gap, n_survivors).

    The locked doctrine: min-AIC survivor wins ONLY when it beats the
    runner-up survivor by >= daic; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. A single survivor
    wins by default (nothing to be confused with)."""
    sv = survivors(row, cols, daic)
    if not sv:
        return 'INCONCLUSIVE', float('nan'), 0
    order = sorted(sv.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
    if len(order) == 1:
        return order[0][0], float('inf'), 1
    gap = order[1][1] - order[0][1]
    if gap >= daic:
        return order[0][0], gap, len(order)
    return 'INCONCLUSIVE', gap, len(order)


def class_gated_winner(row, cols, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """(class_winner | 'INCONCLUSIVE', best_prefix_in_class, cross_class_gap,
    n_members_within_gate).

    Level-2 doctrine: each degeneracy CLASS is represented by its best (min
    AIC) gated survivor; the top-two gap is evaluated ACROSS classes. A class
    wins even when its members are internally indistinguishable — that
    internal degeneracy is returned as n_members_within (members of the
    winning class within `daic` of its best, i.e. how many flavors the data
    cannot separate)."""
    sv = survivors(row, cols, daic)
    if not sv:
        return 'INCONCLUSIVE', None, float('nan'), 0
    best_by_class = {}
    for p, aic in sv.items():
        c = class_of(p)
        if c not in best_by_class or aic < best_by_class[c][1]:
            best_by_class[c] = (p, aic)
    order = sorted(best_by_class.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][1])
    cname, (bp, baic) = order[0]
    members_within = sum(1 for p, a in sv.items()
                         if class_of(p) == cname and (a - baic) <= daic)
    if len(order) == 1:
        return cname, bp, float('inf'), members_within
    gap = order[1][1][1] - baic
    if gap >= daic:
        return cname, bp, gap, members_within
    return 'INCONCLUSIVE', bp, gap, members_within


def burst_admission(table, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """BURST-LEVEL component admission (adopted by Vikas 2026-07-29; modeled on
    Burgess+2014 ApJ 784:17 §3.4, whose BB entered a burst's analysis only if
    it improved C-stat by >=10 in at least one bin — then was fit in EVERY bin).

    A composite is ADMITTED for this burst when >= 1 bin has it as a
    chain-gated survivor: VALID + STATUS OK + finite AIC + beats EVERY nested
    parent by >= daic (survivors() enforces exactly this). Admission does NOT
    require winning the bin — improvement over the parents suffices, per
    Burgess. Purpose: evolution/correlation studies (kT(t), Ep–kT, EC(t)) use
    the admitted-burst TRACKS across all bins instead of re-selecting bin by
    bin — mitigating the per-bin detectability selection that can imprint
    spurious parameter correlations. The strict per-bin census is unchanged.

    Returns {composite_prefix: n_bins_passing} for admitted composites."""
    cols = table.colnames
    counts = {}
    for r in table:
        try:
            blk = int(r['BLOCK'])
        except Exception:
            continue
        if blk < 0:
            continue                              # T_INT row
        for p in survivors(r, cols, daic):
            if p in PARENTS:                      # composites only
                counts[p] = counts.get(p, 0) + 1
    return counts


def component_track(table, prefix, param_cols, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """Per-block parameter track for an (admitted) component: one entry per
    science bin with the requested parameter values/errors and a CONSTRAINED
    flag (VALID + STATUS OK + finite AIC in that bin — i.e. non-railed).
    Unconstrained bins are RETAINED, flagged False — the Burgess construction
    tracks the component everywhere and lets the flag carry the honesty.

    param_cols: iterable of column suffixes, e.g. ('KT', 'EP').
    Returns list of dicts: {block, t_mid, constrained, <col>: (val, err)}."""
    cols = table.colnames
    out = []
    for r in table:
        try:
            blk = int(r['BLOCK'])
        except Exception:
            continue
        if blk < 0:
            continue
        entry = {'block': blk,
                 't_mid': float(r['T_MID']) if 'T_MID' in cols else float('nan'),
                 'constrained': is_valid(r, prefix, cols)}
        for c in param_cols:
            v = _val(r, f'{prefix}_{c}')
            e = _val(r, f'{prefix}_{c}_ERR')
            entry[c] = (v, e)
        out.append(entry)
    return out


def census(tables, daic=DAIC_GATE):
    """Population census over astropy Tables of spectral_fits rows.

    Returns dict with per-block winners list, counts by model and family,
    and the ambiguity statistics the paper must headline."""
    winners = []
    for trig, t in tables:
        cols = t.colnames
        for r in t:
            try:
                blk = int(r['BLOCK'])
            except Exception:
                continue
            if blk < 0:
                continue                       # T_INT row
            w, gap, nsv = gated_winner(r, cols, daic)
            cw, cbest, cgap, cwithin = class_gated_winner(r, cols, daic)
            winners.append({'trigger': trig, 'block': blk,
                            'winner': w, 'top2_gap': gap, 'n_survivors': nsv,
                            'class_winner': cw, 'class_best_model': cbest,
                            'class_gap': cgap, 'class_members_within': cwithin})
    from collections import Counter
    by_model = Counter(w['winner'] for w in winners)
    by_class = Counter(w['class_winner'] for w in winners)
    by_family = Counter(
        MODELS[w['winner']][1] if w['winner'] in MODELS else 'inconclusive'
        for w in winners)
    n = len(winners)
    n_inc = by_model.get('INCONCLUSIVE', 0)
    n_cinc = by_class.get('INCONCLUSIVE', 0)
    # blocks where the CLASS is decisive but the exact flavor is not — the
    # "shape known, flavor degenerate" population (Vikas 2026-07-18)
    n_flavor_deg = sum(1 for w in winners
                       if w['class_winner'] != 'INCONCLUSIVE'
                       and w['winner'] == 'INCONCLUSIVE')
    return {
        'n_blocks': n,
        'n_inconclusive': n_inc,
        'frac_inconclusive': (n_inc / n) if n else float('nan'),
        'n_class_inconclusive': n_cinc,
        'frac_class_inconclusive': (n_cinc / n) if n else float('nan'),
        'n_flavor_degenerate': n_flavor_deg,
        'by_model': dict(by_model),
        'by_class': dict(by_class),
        'by_family': dict(by_family),
        'winners': winners,
    }


if __name__ == '__main__':

    from astropy.table import Table
    tabs = [(f.split('/')[-2], Table.read(f, format='ascii.ecsv'))
            for f in sys.argv[1:]]

     1	# Skill: Temporal (Step 7) — T90/T50, MVT, lag, pulse fits
     2	
     3	**Purpose:** the per-burst temporal measurements (durations, minimum variability timescale,
     4	spectral lag, pulse morphology) from the SAME approved Stage-1 selections that drive the
     5	spectroscopy. **Audience:** anyone running `scripts/40_temporal_survey.py` or reading
     6	`results/temporal_catalog_human.ecsv`.
     7	**⚠ STATUS: the weakest step of the pipeline.** Codex's audit verdict — the temporal numbers
     8	*"should not be used scientifically"* until the defects below are fixed — stands. This skill
     9	documents the method AND the defect ledger; quoting a temporal number without checking the
    10	ledger is a fake pass.
    11	
    12	## Inputs
    13	```yaml
    14	trigger:   bn<XXXXXXXXX>
    15	stage1:    results/background_intervals.ecsv    # approved dets + bkg windows
    16	data:      data/<trigger>/glg_tte_<refNaI>_*    # reference NaI TTE
    17	env:       LIGHT tier (numpy/astropy) — no threeML needed
    18	chain:     ~/Desktop/Projects/GRB_Handbook_Project/grb_pipeline/analysis/temporal.py
    19	           (vendored handbook: analyze_single_pulse = T90 -> MVT -> lag -> pulse)
    20	```
    21	
    22	## Outputs
    23	`results/temporal_catalog_human.ecsv` — one row per burst: T90/T50 (+errs), MVT-Haar, lag,
    24	Gowri pulse parameters (A, s_l, s_r, r_l, r_r), φ = s_l/s_r, R², class.
    25	
    26	## The four measurements
    27	1. **T90/T50** — cumulative background-subtracted counts between 5%/95% (25%/75%);
    28	   errors by **Poisson mock light curves (n=200, time order preserved; T90 formed per
    29	   realization so the t5/t95 covariance is included)** — fixed 2026-08-13, see defect ledger.
    30	2. **MVT** — Haar-wavelet cross-check in this chain; the CANONICAL MVT is Bala's
    31	   `mvt_runner` run separately (the upstream Bala code was NOT adoptable unmodified —
    32	   repaired fork; the old classifier is quarantined; LATBright-era MVT MC numbers are
    33	   unsafe. Memory: `project_mvt_audit_2026-07-18`).
    34	3. **Spectral lag** — asymmetric-Gaussian peak of the band-band CCF, Monte-Carlo errors.
    35	   ⚠ **SIGN CONVENTION INVERTED — see defect ledger.**
    36	4. **Pulse fit** — the Gowri+2025 two-sigmoid:
    37	   `I(t) = (A/4)·[1−tanh((t−r_r)/s_r)]·[1+tanh((t−r_l)/s_l)]`, asymmetry φ = s_l/s_r
    38	   (φ<1 = FRED-like). Protocol adopted EXACTLY from the paper: rebin to ≤300 bins
    39	   (`_GOWRI_MAX_BINS`), accept only R² ≥ 0.7 (`_GOWRI_R2_MIN`), and **require r_l ≤ r_r**
    40	   — the handoff that said `r_l ≥ r_r` was wrong and would have collapsed every pulse
    41	   (caught against the paper verbatim: *"we always require rl ≤ rr"*). Fit `dr = r_r − r_l ≥ 0`
    42	   as the parameter, never the raw pair.
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# full-sample survey (12-core cap):
    46	python scripts/40_temporal_survey.py
    47	```
    48	
    49	## Frame rule: T90 is BAND-DEPENDENT — correct before diffing (Qin+2013, verified 2026-08-09)
    50	Comprehensive Analysis III (`2013ApJ...763...15Q`, published PDF on disk) measures
    51	**T̄₉₀ ∝ E^(−0.20 ± 0.02)** for long GRBs across six GBM sub-bands. Consequence: a harder-band
    52	instrument reports a SHORTER duration for the same burst, lawfully.
    53	Live demonstration (bn090530760): GBM catalog 157.7 s (8–1000 keV) vs Suzaku-WAM 113 s
    54	(50 keV–5 MeV). Band-centre ratio ⇒ predicted factor ≈ 0.72; observed 113/157.7 = **0.72**.
    55	What looked like three inconsistent durations was one burst obeying one power law.
    56	**RULE:** never diff a published T90 against ours without the E^−0.2 band correction (an L21
    57	frame-alignment item with a number attached). Cite Qin+2013; note their caveat that bright-burst
    58	samples give steeper (−0.4, Bissaldi+2011).
    59	
    60	### ⚠ CORRECTION (Vikas's Qin reading, 2026-08-13; PDF-verified same day)
    61	**The exponent is a POPULATION-MEAN relation, not a per-burst law.** Their §Figure 7 fits
    62	`T̄₉₀` — the *sample mean* T90 — against the central energy of each band; the slope
    63	−0.20 ± 0.02 describes how the population average moves, and says nothing about the scatter
    64	of any single burst around it. Our rule above applies it to INDIVIDUAL bursts (bn090530760
    65	matched to 0.72 — a good outcome, but one draw from a distribution whose width we never
    66	measured).
    67	**Consequences, binding from now on:**
    68	1. A band-corrected T90 diff is a CONSISTENCY CHECK with population-level scatter attached,
    69	   never a precision prediction. Never call a residual mismatch a discrepancy on the strength
    70	   of E^−0.20 alone.
    71	2. To use it per-burst we must measure the per-burst relation ourselves — `scripts/40` already
    72	   computes T90 per band, so the campaign's own multi-band T90s give both the population slope
    73	   AND its scatter. Do that before the frozen numbers are quoted.
    74	3. **Their T90 is count-space by their own statement** — verbatim: *"Our calculation is done
    75	   purely in count space. Since the GBM is constantly slewing in orbit, this method could skew
    76	   the T90 estimation for long GRBs."* The GBM catalog instead accumulates response-corrected
    77	   photon fluence. So a Qin-vs-catalog T90 difference can be METHOD, not band (a T9-class
    78	   coverage/estimator distinction). Label which space every harvested T90 lives in.
    79	4. Source audits (resolved 2026-08-13 against the PDF; full record in skill reference 22):
    80	   the HR "inconsistency" is **under-signposting, not contradiction** — the 25–50 keV
    81	   denominator is quoted as the legacy BATSE definition (Kouveliotou+1993), the Fig. 4 caption
    82	   states the 50–100 keV denominator actually plotted for GBM; their GBM hardness is
    83	   model-derived from GCN spectral parameters, not counts. The `091010`/`090910` clash is a
    84	   CAPTION typo (text + panel label say 091010). The short:long ratio 1:6.5 (39:253) is
    85	   internally consistent. **Genuinely open:** Table 2's soft-band P_KMM (2.25e−2, 5.9e−4)
    86	   reject one Gaussian under their own `P<0.05` rule while the text says bimodality is
    87	   rejected — do not inherit; and the paper NEVER states its Bayesian-block fitness function
    88	   or prior, so Figure 1 is not reproducible from the paper alone.
    89	5. Their σ_T90 combines separate t5/t95 Monte Carlo spreads in quadrature; t5 and t95 come
    90	   from the SAME cumulative light curve and are correlated. Our MC must form
    91	   `T90^(j) = t95^(j) − t5^(j)` per realization and take the spread of that distribution
    92	   directly (covariance included by construction). Check `scripts/40`'s estimator against this
    93	   before quoting any T90 error.
    94	
    95	## L26 — LAG SIGN is a systematic trap: state the convention, verify against a known burst  *(2026-08-10)*
    96	Two independent instances, one ours and one published:
    97	1. **Ours:** the handbook lag sign is INVERTED (defect ledger above) — caught only by cross-check.
    98	2. **Lu+2018 (`2018ApJ...865..153L`), published ApJ, verified in the PDF:** the text states t_p is
    99	   *"negatively related to the photon energy E"* — i.e. HIGH energy peaks EARLIER, low energy later,
   100	   the conventional positive lag — and then the very next sentence says the opposite: *"the pulse
   101	   profile in a lower energy band tends to **peak earlier**"*. One of the two is wrong; the trend
   102	   statement and their own positive τ̂₃₁ values (e.g. +7.08 s for bn090530760) say the sentence is.
   103	
   104	Two instances make it a class, not a slip. Sign errors survive refereeing because both conventions
   105	are "obvious" to their users and neither is usually written down.
   106	**RULE:** (a) every quoted lag carries its convention explicitly — *positive lag = low-energy
   107	photons arrive LATER* is ours; (b) validate the pipeline's sign on a burst with an unambiguous
   108	published direction before any lag science; (c) when diffing a published lag, check the paper's
   109	OWN internal consistency (trend statement vs prose vs table sign) rather than assuming.
   110	**TEST:** `test_L26_lag_sign_on_reference_burst` — pending the handbook sign fix.

   133	- **Bootstrap error > value** means the bootstrap is resampling noise, not the burst — treat as

   136	  ratio — do not diff against Norris asymmetries without a mapping.
   137	- **Lag–MVT plans**: this territory is a REDO, not a discovery (Sonbas+2013; Göktaş+2025
   138	  slope 1.01) — see memory `project_lagmvt_is_a_redo` before proposing science here.

    50	Yes---today with a human at the gate, and the gate is the training
    51	apparatus, not the ceiling. Analyzing a
    52	gamma-ray burst (GRB) is mostly judgement calls: which detectors to trust,
    53	where the background sits, where the burst starts and stops, how finely to
    54	slice it in time, and which of two dozen spectral models to believe.
    55	We describe a system that makes those calls, and we are precise about its
    56	architecture: it is not an autonomous agent but a \emph{gated workflow with
    57	bounded agency}---predefined analysis paths in which an AI makes named,
    58	auditable decisions (model selection, fit validity, literature verification,
    59	mismatch attribution) while a human approves every step, and every approval
    60	is stamped. The system's knowledge lives in a \emph{Skill Library}: versioned
    61	plain-language procedure documents that any AI agent---or any student---can
    62	read and execute. The Library is not documentation; it is the system's
    63	memory, and it learns. Each burst is analyzed blind, reconciled against the
    64	published literature, and every mismatch is attributed---our error, the
    65	literature's, or a difference of frames---and distilled into a numbered
    66	lesson that ships with an executable test, so that no lesson can be silently
    67	forgotten. Applied to a campaign over 106 single-pulse \textit{Fermi}/GBM
    68	bursts, the first ten walkthroughs\prov{} produced twenty-seven such lessons,
    69	found and fixed five engine defects (one of which---a validity gate whose
    70	linear margin silently disqualified soft spectra---would have biased the
    71	census toward spurious thermal components), confirmed blind predictions
    72	drawn from the literature, and refuted one of its own. The learning curve
    73	(lessons per burst) is the paper's central figure: the campaign trains a
    74	pipeline, not model weights, and the trained artifact is readable, testable,
    75	and transfers between AI systems. We report where the agent cannot yet
    76	be trusted---adjudicating contested verdicts, where panels of AI reviewers
    77	prove to be strong \emph{generators} of checkable findings but weak
    78	\emph{adjudicators}, their unanimity sometimes an artifact of shared priors
    79	rather than independent measurement---and we are explicit that this boundary
    80	is a statement about the current point on the learning curve, not about AI
    81	in principle: every gate correction is itself distilled into the Library, so
    82	the human's judgment is being transferred, not merely exercised, and the
    83	measurable question is whether the gates go quiet. We release the Skill
    84	Library, the engine, the tests, and the per-burst records.
    85	\end{abstract}
    86

    88	Astronomy software (1855) --- Astrostatistics (1882)}

    90	% ===========================================================================
    91	\section{Introduction} \label{sec:intro}
    92	% ===========================================================================
    93	
    94	The question in our title is usually asked as if it had a yes-or-no answer.
    95	It does not, because ``AI doing analysis'' names at least two different
    96	architectures, and the difference between them decides what the answer can
    97	mean. In the first architecture, a \emph{workflow}, the analysis follows
    98	predefined paths---the same stages, in the same order, for every burst---and
    99	software executes them. In the second, an \emph{agent}, a model directs its
   100	own process: it decides what to do next, which tools to call, and when it is
   101	finished \citep{anthropic2024agents}. Workflows are auditable and dull; agents are
   102	flexible and hard to trust. Most claims that ``AI analyzed the data'' blur
   103	the two.
   104	
   105	This paper builds and tests a deliberate hybrid, and names it honestly: a
   106	\emph{gated workflow with bounded agency}. The analysis pipeline---data
   107	acquisition, detector and background selection, adaptive binning, spectral
   108	fitting, temporal analysis, quality control---is a workflow: its stages are
   109	fixed, its statistics are chosen in advance, and its outputs are stamped
   110	with provenance. Inside that workflow, an AI exercises agency at exactly the
   111	points where judgement is required and we can afford to audit it: which of
   112	twenty-four spectral models wins a gated comparison, whether a fit is valid
   113	or sits on a parameter rail, whether a published value has been verified at
   114	its source, and---when our numbers disagree with the literature---whether the
   115	fault is ours, theirs, or a difference of analysis frames. A human approves
   116	every step before the next one runs. Nothing advances on silence, and no
   117	approval is ever fabricated: every decision carries a stamp naming who, or
   118	what, made it.
   119	
   120	Why is time-resolved GRB spectroscopy the right testbed rather than a
   121	convenient one? Because it concentrates, in one measurement problem, the
   122	three features that make scientific AI hard to evaluate. First, the
   123	decisions have no answer key. Two careful published analyses of the same
   124	burst, using overlapping data and defensible methods, can disagree about
   125	whether a thermal component exists at all; the literature is a
   126	\emph{distribution} over defensible choices, not a ground truth
   127	\citep{2022ApJ...938..159S,2019ApJ...887...13F}. Second, the instrument
   128	matters: responses age, detectors are occulted, backgrounds are fit, and a
   129	systematic that is invisible in one regime of burst brightness or hardness
   130	appears only when the sample happens to present the other. Third, the
   131	stakes are population-level: our science application is a census of
   132	spectral shapes across 106 single-pulse bursts selected morphologically
   133	\citep{2024ApJ...972...83B}, and a small per-burst bias becomes a
   134	population-level artifact. A system that merely \emph{runs} on such data is
   135	easy; a system whose outputs deserve trust must show its work at every one
   136	of these pressure points.
   137	
   138	Our design answer, developed in \S\ref{sec:workflow}, has one unusual
   139	component that we believe is the paper's main methodological contribution.
   140	The system's procedural knowledge lives in a \emph{Skill Library}: versioned,
   280	agent's own results are frozen---written to the Burst Record in a form that
   281	cannot be revised---together with predictions derived from the harvested
   282	literature (\S\ref{sec:verify}). Only then are the two compared, and every
   283	mismatch is pushed to one of three attributions: \emph{we-wrong} (an error on
   284	our side, which must be fixed and tested), \emph{they-wrong} (a documented
   285	problem in the published analysis, stated with evidence), or
   286	\emph{frame-difference} (both analyses defensible; the difference traced to
   287	conventions, data selections, or eras, and recorded as a normalization rule).
   288	The attribution, not the mismatch, is the product: it becomes a numbered
   289	lesson in the Skill Library, shipped with an executable test
   290	(\S\ref{sec:learning}).
   291	
   292	The loop's exit condition is convergence: when $K$ consecutive bursts
   293	complete without producing a single new lesson, the Skill Library is declared
   294	converged, the pipeline is frozen at a recorded commit, and the entire
   295	106-burst sample is re-analyzed once, from scratch, by the frozen system.
   296	Only that production sweep produces citable numbers; every value in this
   297	paper from the campaign era carries the provisional flag\prov. The design
   298	premise, stated plainly: \emph{the per-burst numbers are not the product;
   299	the matured Skill Library is.}
   300	
   301	\subsection{Inside the fitting step} \label{sec:fitstep}
   302	
   303	The fitting engine confronts each time bin with twenty-four spectral models:
   304	four one-break continua, five carrying extra low-energy structure (thermal
   305	or a second break), and fifteen high-energy composites. Three rules govern
   306	what the numbers may mean. First, \emph{inclusion is gated on data quality,
   307	never on detection significance}: every detector band with usable data and a
   308	valid response enters the joint fit, because conditioning inclusion on
   309	significance manufactures spurious detections in exactly the bursts where a
   310	band fluctuated upward. Second, \emph{every model family receives
   311	unconditional multistarts}, because a chained seed from a bright epoch can
   312	strand a faint bin in a wrong local minimum---a failure we document in
   313	\S\ref{sec:learning}. Third, \emph{validity gates} exclude from model
   314	selection any fit whose shape parameters sit on a bound, with the margins
   315	computed in the parameter's natural geometry (logarithmic for
   316	energy-like parameters spanning decades)---a rule the campaign itself had to
   317	learn, at measurable cost, from its first soft burst.
   318	
   319	Model comparison is then reported as evidence, not verdicts: the winning
   320	model's margin is quoted both against the runner-up (\emph{which} model) and
   321	against the best one-break continuum (\emph{is extra structure needed at
   322	all}), each converted to an evidence ratio $e^{\Delta\mathrm{AIC}/2}$ and
   323	graded. A margin of 6 corresponds to roughly 20:1 and is called strong;
   324	10, roughly 150:1, decisive; anything less is reported as what it is. Where
   325	extra structure is required but thermal and non-thermal descriptions sit
   326	within a few units of each other, the bin is assigned to a degeneracy class
   327	rather than a physics claim: \emph{adequacy and identity are different
   328	questions}, and the second frequently cannot be answered from these data
   329	alone.
   330	
   331	\subsection{Who decides what} \label{sec:authority}
   332	
   333	\begin{deluxetable*}{lll}
   334	\tablecaption{The authority split: who decides what.\label{tab:authority}}
   335	\tablehead{\colhead{the workflow decides (predefined)} & \colhead{the AI decides (bounded agency)} & \colhead{the human decides (gates)}}
   336	\startdata
   337	step order and Protocol & model winner via the gated comparison & scope and completion contract \\
   338	energy selections; statistic & fit-validity verdicts & every Stage-1 selection (stamped) \\
   339	multistart seeds; bound gates & literature verification and frame alignment & every step gate \\
   340	provenance stamping & mismatch attribution; lesson drafting & lesson acceptance; convergence; freeze \\
   341	typed terminal states & anomaly flagging and escalation & promotion from the discovery plane; every claim \\
   342	\enddata
   343	\end{deluxetable*}
   344	
   345	Table~\ref{tab:authority} states the paper's honesty contract. The
   346	\emph{workflow} decides everything decided in advance: the step order, the
   347	energy selections, the statistic, the multistart seeds, the stamping of
   348	provenance. The \emph{AI} decides, within audited bounds: which model wins
   349	the gated comparison, whether a fit is valid, whether a published value has
   350	been verified at source and in which frame, how a mismatch is attributed,
   351	and which anomalies deserve escalation. The \emph{human} decides everything
   352	consequential: the scope, every step gate, whether a proposed lesson enters
   353	the Library, when convergence is declared, and every scientific claim that
   354	leaves the system. In ten bursts\prov{} of operation, no approval was ever
   355	generated by the system on the human's behalf; the reverse---the human
   356	overruling the agent's proposal---occurred repeatedly and is part of the
   357	record (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
   358	
   359	\subsection{Two planes} \label{sec:planes}
   360	
   361	Everything above describes the \emph{production plane}. A second,
   362	\emph{discovery plane} exists for ideas that do not belong inside a frozen
   363	workflow: anomalies that suggest new observables, hypotheses formed after
   364	seeing data. Work there is sandboxed and carries no evidentiary weight until
   365	it passes a promotion gate---calibration on simulations, validation on data
   366	that did not motivate it, human approval. The governing rule is stated once
   367	and enforced always: \emph{the agent may invent a new scorecard after seeing
   368	the game; it may not pretend the scorecard was chosen before the game.}
   369	
   370	\subsection{The doctrine} \label{sec:doctrine}
   371	
   372	Seven rules, each purchased by a documented failure, govern all of the
   373	above: (1) analyze blind first---published values are harvested before
   374	fitting but the fit is never steered toward them; (2) margins are computed
   375	over valid fits only; (3) evidence ratios, never bare verdicts; (4)
   376	inclusion by data quality, never significance---and its absolute corollary:
   377	production fits never drop data that passes the quality gate, with/without
   378	refits are attribution diagnostics whose data-dropped member can never be
   379	quoted as a result, and omission of data is legal only through a documented
   380	quality exclusion; (5) a lesson is not learned
   381	until it is a claim \emph{and} a test; (6) no silent approvals---a skipped
   382	check is a fake pass; (7) verify claims at their source, and attribute
   383	agreement or disagreement at the level of shared primitives. The failures
   384	that funded each rule appear in \S\ref{sec:learning} and
   385	\S\ref{sec:discussion}.
   386	
   387	% ===========================================================================
   388	\section{Learning Without Gradients} \label{sec:learning}
   389	% ===========================================================================
   390	Contemporary AI agents are improved in five ways: pretraining on large
   391	corpora; supervised fine-tuning on demonstration trajectories; preference
   392	optimization against human or model judgments; reinforcement learning on
   393	\emph{verifiable} rewards, where a trajectory is reinforced only if its
   394	outcome can be checked mechanically (code passing tests, proofs verifying);
   395	and \emph{harness-side learning}, in which the model's weights are never
   396	touched and the surrounding harness---its instructions, procedures, and
   397	memory---accumulates capability instead \citep{2025Natur.645..633G,2023arXiv230516291W,2023arXiv230311366S}. Our
   398	campaign is training of the fifth kind carrying the fourth kind's essential
   399	ingredient. The weights of every model we use are frozen; the artifact that
   400	learns is the Skill Library; and the unit of learning is constrained to be
   401	\emph{verifiable}: a lesson enters the Library only as a claim with
   402	provenance (which burst, which date, which evidence) together with an
   403	executable test, added to the Lesson Test-Suite, that fails if the lesson is
   404	ever violated again. The suite runs against the current analysis products;
   405	where a table predates a fix, the corresponding failure is registered in a
   406	known-stale ledger with its clearing condition rather than silenced---debt is
   407	visible, never normalized.
   408	
   409	This training style has properties that gradient methods cannot offer at our
   410	scale, and one property they share. It is data-efficient: the first ten
   411	bursts\prov{} produced twenty-seven numbered lessons. It is auditable: the
   412	learned policy is markdown, and every rule cites the burst that paid for it.
   413	It transfers across model families: the same Library is executed by
   414	different vendors' agents, which is the basis of the multi-system benchmark
   415	of \S\ref{sec:design}. It survives model upgrades. And---the shared
   416	property---it exhibits a learning curve (Fig.~\ref{fig:curve}), whose
   417	flattening is the campaign's stopping criterion: when $K$ consecutive bursts
   418	produce no new lesson, the Library is converged and the pipeline is frozen.
   419	
   420	\begin{figure}[t]
   421	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{campaign_learning_curve.png}
   422	\caption{The campaign learning curve\prov: lessons distilled per burst
   423	(bars), engine defects found (dark bars), and the cumulative lesson count
   424	(line) across the first eight walked bursts. The curve is visibly
   425	unconverged; its flattening, not a preset burst count, terminates the
   426	training phase.}
   427	\label{fig:curve}
   428	\end{figure}
   429	
   430	Two episodes illustrate what the loop learns and how. The first is a defect
   431	we designate L27. The engine's validity gates flagged a fitted parameter as
   432	railed when it sat within a fixed \emph{linear} margin of its bound. For
   433	energy-like parameters bounded across three decades, that linear margin is
   434	an absolute dead zone of tens of keV above the lower bound---and every burst
   435	analyzed in the campaign's first seven walkthroughs had a peak energy far
   436	above it. The eighth burst was soft ($\Ep\!\sim\!50$--140~keV\prov), and the
   437	gate silently disqualified \emph{every} one-break continuum in most of its
   438	time bins, delivering the blocks to thermal-composite models by forfeit.
   439	Uncorrected, the census would have manufactured a population-level
   440	correlation between spectral softness and thermal components---a selection
   441	bias wearing the costume of physics. The repair (margins computed in the
   442	parameter's natural geometry), its unit test, and the burst's refit happened
   443	within the same session; the pre/post contrast---most blocks ``preferring''
   444	extra structure before, none after\prov---is the measured size of the bias
   445	the lesson prevents. The episode is also an argument about curricula:
   446	the defect was invisible until the sample's serial ordering happened to
   447	deliver a soft burst, so \emph{regime coverage, not burst count, is what a
   448	training sample must supply}.
   449	
   450	The second episode is a cross-validation. Our temporal chain carried a
   451	known, ledgered defect: a spectral-lag sign convention inverted with respect
   452	to the field's standard. The eighth burst has a published lag of
   453	$+7.08\pm0.45$~s in the conventional sign \citep{2018ApJ...865..153L}; our
   454	chain returned $-5.99$~s\prov. Same burst, same physical direction, opposite
   455	sign: the ledgered inversion was confirmed against external ground truth in
   456	the course of ordinary operations, and the lesson (state the convention with
   457	every quoted lag; validate the sign against a burst with a published
   458	direction) was distilled with the defect still unfixed at source---the
   459	Library records what is \emph{known}, including known-broken.
   460	
   520	too}: the adversary claimed a nondeterministic fitting step; five identical
   521	reruns showed spread exactly zero\prov---its variance had been its own
   522	varying invocations. Second, with/without-data refits are attribution
   523	diagnostics only; a data-dropped fit is never evidence for a claim
   524	(\S\ref{sec:doctrine}).
   525	
   526	% ===========================================================================
   527	\section{Experimental Design: Human versus Agent} \label{sec:design}
   528	% ===========================================================================
   529	The benchmark design retains v1's core: a 25-burst subset receives
   530	independent Stage-1 selections from experienced researchers, and agents from
   531	multiple vendors---executing the \emph{same} Skill Library, so that
   532	differences isolate the model rather than the prompt---are scored not on
   533	matching any single expert but on landing within the \emph{spread of the
   534	experts}, decision by decision: detector sets, background windows, source
   535	intervals, model verdicts. Scoring decisions rather than published numbers
   536	is forced on us by the field itself: published analyses of the same burst
   537	disagree, so the literature is a distribution over defensible choices and
   538	cannot serve as an answer key. \PENDING{the multi-system benchmark run; a
   539	second independent expert completes the human spread}
   540	
   541	Operations have since added a second, naturally-occurring arm: the sample's
   542	post-2020 bursts are walked by a human collaborator while the 2015--2019
   543	range is walked by the agent-operated workflow described here, both under
   544	the same Protocol. Inter-operator consistency on the shared methodology
   545	becomes a benchmark denominator that no bespoke exercise could provide.
   546	
   547	% ===========================================================================
   548	\section{Walkthrough-Era Results} \label{sec:results}
   549	% ===========================================================================
   550	All numbers in this section are walkthrough-era and provisional\prov;
   551	they will be regenerated by the frozen production sweep. Ten bursts have
   552	been walked. Among them: a burst whose apparent two-break ``decisive''
   553	margin traced to a railed reference model and now carries a capped-bound
   554	stamp; a burst whose published photospheric identification our wider menu
   555	reduces to a forced choice between statistically equivalent thermal and
   556	non-thermal descriptions; a burst in which the fitted low-energy break and
   557	the fitted blackbody peak track each other at the few-percent level across
   558	eleven bins---one spectral feature wearing two model names; the campaign's
   559	first soft burst (the L27 episode), whose positive low-energy slopes are
   560	carried entirely by one-break continua; the campaign's first
   561	intensity-tracking burst, whose blind $\Ep$ track follows the flux and whose
   562	late-time cutoff evolution sits in open, documented tension with a published
   563	constant-$\Gamma$ curvature interpretation; and the field's best-known
   564	polarimetric burst, for which published polarization-angle rotations enter
   565	the frozen predictions as constraints from an instrument we do not fit.
   566	The Campaign Ledger records, per burst: lessons born, defects found,
   567	blind-prediction outcomes, and human gate corrections; it is released with
   568	the paper, and Fig.~\ref{fig:curve} is computed from it. External,
   569	zero-cost validations accumulated along the way: our adaptive binning
   570	reproduces a published analysis' Bayesian-block edges to three decimal
   571	places on a shared burst \citep{2021ApJS..253...43L}, and twenty-two of our sample's bursts carry
   572	published lag, width, and evolution-class measurements \citep{2018ApJ...865..153L} against which the
   573	temporal chain is validated burst by burst as the campaign reaches them.
   574	
   575	% ===========================================================================
   576	\section{Discussion} \label{sec:discussion}
   577	% ===========================================================================
   578	\subsection{Failure taxonomy} \label{sec:failures}
   579	
   580	Every mode below was observed in this campaign, caught, and converted into
   581	doctrine; none was caught by the failing agent itself.
   582	\emph{Over-claiming}: three retracted claims, each computed from technically
   583	correct numbers whose validity flags had not been checked; caught by the
   584	human gate and by an independent agent audit. \emph{Prescribed unanimity}:
   585	a panel's unanimous verdict traced verbatim to the shared prior document
   586	(\S\ref{sec:verify}). \emph{Confabulation}: a reviewer channel reporting
   587	statistics absent from its own assigned figure. \emph{Estimator mismatch}:
   588	an ad-hoc quality check using a simpler background model than production,
   589	manufacturing a $5.6\sigma$ alarm against a selection a human had already,
   590	correctly, approved---the rule is that a check must use the production
   591	estimator or it is not a check. \emph{Tool-interface drift}: invoking one's
   592	own tools with invented arguments. \emph{Momentum skips}: advancing past a
   593	presentation step the Protocol requires; caught by the human, converted
   594	into an explicit rule. \emph{Diagnostic-becomes-result drift}: treating a
   595	data-dropped sensitivity refit as evidence (\S\ref{sec:doctrine}).
   596	The taxonomy is the practical answer to ``where does the agent still need a
   597	human'': at every point where the system's own priors, momentum, or
   598	plausible-but-unchecked numbers are the failure mode, because those are
   599	precisely the failures self-review does not catch.
   600	
   601	\subsection{The capability boundary}
   602	
   603	The same experiments that expose these failures locate the boundary
   604	positively: differently-primed AI reviewers are strong \emph{generators} of
   605	checkable findings---several entered the engine as permanent guards---and
   606	weak \emph{adjudicators} of contested verdicts. We therefore spend agency
   607	where generation pays (proposing, localizing, refuting, attributing) and
   608	reserve adjudication for the gated human, with the audit trail as the
   609	interface between them.
   610	
   611	\subsection{Outlook: the discovery plane, and creativity as graph operations}
   612	\label{sec:creativity}
   613	
   614	The production plane described in this paper deliberately excludes open-ended
   615	discovery; a second, sandboxed plane exists for it, governed by one rule:
   616	the agent may invent a new scorecard after seeing the game, but may not
   617	pretend the scorecard was chosen before the game. What would make that plane
   618	\emph{generative} rather than merely permitted? We close with a hypothesis
   619	we are developing and have begun to stress-test: that creative scientific
   620	acts are, predominantly, typed operations on the knowledge graph of the
   621	literature---\textbf{A$'$}, drawing an edge along a long, archivally stale,
   622	or never-co-cited path between semantically compatible regions;
   623	\textbf{B$'$}, negating a \emph{named, load-bearing assumption} of a
   624	specific published derivation, as the first generative move rather than as a
   625	consequence of new data; and \textbf{C}, constructing a new graph element
   626	outright---a phenomenon-node, a question, a topology of existing components.
   627	An adversarial audit of this taxonomy against twenty-four historically
   628	recognized discoveries found the two-class version (A$'$, B$'$) insufficient
   629	---class C is required, and the classification must apply to \emph{acts},
   630	not results (a landmark observation can contain no creative jump)---while
   631	identifying a genuinely open architectural slot: a literature-scale
   632	knowledge graph in which each result carries its derivation assumptions as
   633	first-class metadata, with negation as a provenance-tracked generative
   634	operator \citep{boden2004,swanson1986,2013Sci...342..468U,2013arXiv1302.6906F,wiggins2006}. The
   635	Reconciliation Protocol already extracts, burst by burst, exactly the
   636	assumption-level statements such a graph requires; the discovery plane is
   637	where they will compound.
   638	
   639	\subsection{What generalizes}
   640	
   641	Gates with stamps, lessons-as-tests, blind-first frozen predictions,
   642	frame-alignment before any diff, independence-at-the-primitive, and the
   643	failure taxonomy are domain-agnostic and export as a package; the engine,
   644	the menu, and the lessons' content are the domain deposit that makes the
   645	package worth executing. Both are released.
   646	
   647	% ===========================================================================
   648	\section{Conclusions} \label{sec:conclusions}
   649	% ===========================================================================
   650	Yes---as a gated workflow with bounded agency, trained harness-side under
   651	verifiable lessons, and audited by a doctrine that treats agreement with
   652	suspicion and refutation as a service. The system analyzed ten bursts\prov{}
   653	end to end, taught itself twenty-seven durable lessons, found five of its own
   654	engine defects including one census-grade selection bias, validated a known
   655	defect against published ground truth, and refuted one of its own frozen
   656	predictions. The per-burst numbers are provisional by design; the Skill
   657	Library is not. When the learning curve flattens, the pipeline freezes and
   658	runs the full sample once; that sweep, not this paper, produces the census.
   659	The question in the title has an honest answer only with its architecture
   660	attached---and that architecture, we argue, is the contribution.
   661	
   662	We do not mistake the current boundary for a permanent one. Every failure
   663	mode in \S\ref{sec:failures} was caught at a gate, and every catch became a
   664	lesson: the gates are where human judgment is \emph{transferred}, not merely
   665	exercised, and the Library is the accumulating transfer. The claim that some
   666	capability---taste in ambiguous selections, suspicion of one's own
   667	agreement, the adjudication of contested verdicts---is inherently human is,
   668	under this architecture, an empirical claim about the tail of a learning
   669	curve, testable by whether the gate-correction rate falls to zero as
   670	lessons accumulate. And the curriculum need not stop at analysis: the
   671	discovery-plane operators of \S\ref{sec:creativity}---bridging stale regions
   672	of the literature graph, negating named load-bearing assumptions,
   673	constructing new observables---are mechanisms by which discovery itself
   674	becomes teachable. Whether the gates ever go fully quiet is not something
   675	this paper can assert; it is something this campaign, continued to
   676	convergence and beyond, is built to measure. The gate, in the end, is a
   677	curriculum---and curricula are meant to be completed.
   678	
   679	\appendix
   680	\section{Reproducibility} \label{app:repro}
   681	The release comprises the Skill Library, the engine, the Lesson
   682	Test-Suite, the Campaign Ledger, and the Burst Records, archived with a
   683	DOI \PENDING{Zenodo concept DOI at release}. A fresh clone cannot silently
   684	reproduce our fits: analysis products are regenerated, not shipped, so
   685	reproduction begins at the binning step from tracked inputs; six sample
   686	bursts include tracked raw data. The test suite runs in a base scientific
   687	Python environment; the fitting engine requires the standard \textit{Fermi}
   688	analysis stack.
   689	
   690	\section{Adversarial verification protocol} \label{app:verify}
   691	The protocol: independent reviewer channels are assigned disjoint
   692	evidence primitives and briefed adversarially; an adjudicator with
   693	full access audits every channel's claims against the primary artifacts;
   694	adversary claims are themselves verified by rerun. Results of its first
   695	full execution appear in \S\ref{sec:verify}. A standing per-burst refuter
   696	pass---one honest-refuter agent attacking each Burst Record's verdict before
   697	it closes, its surviving objections recorded in the Record---is the
   698	protocol's next planned extension. \PENDING{refuter pass: pending approval
   699	and first execution}

   462	\section{Verification Doctrine} \label{sec:verify}
   463	% ===========================================================================
   464	\subsection{Blind-first analysis with frozen predictions}
   465	
   466	Before each burst is fitted, the Literature Harvest yields a set of
   467	falsifiable predictions---derived from published analyses, never from our own
   468	outputs---which are frozen alongside a commitment that the fit will not be
   469	steered toward them. The comparison happens only after both sides are
   470	immutable. The campaign's scorecards make the point better than argument.
   471	For the eighth burst, the literature predicted a positive low-energy photon
   472	index early in the burst; our blind fit, with independent binning and a far
   473	larger model menu, reproduced it ($\alpha$ up to $+0.6$\prov). It predicted
   474	monotonic hard-to-soft evolution; our blind $\Ep$ track declined
   475	monotonically\prov. But the natural corollary---that a spectrum this hard
   476	should demand a thermal component---was \emph{refuted}: with the L27-repaired
   477	gates, no time bin required extra structure at even the ``strong'' evidence
   478	grade\prov. A framework that can refute its own frozen expectation is
   479	demonstrating the property that matters; confirmation alone demonstrates
   480	nothing.
   481	
   482	\subsection{Independence lives at the primitive}
   483	
   484	Twice in the campaign, two analyses agreed closely and both were wrong or
   485	both unnecessary: our fitted blackbody temperature agreed with a published
   486	value to five percent while both components were statistically unrequired;
   487	and in the experiment below, two independent review channels built the same
   488	load-bearing argument on the same silently symmetric parameterization,
   489	corroborating each other into a void conclusion. We therefore state the
   490	doctrine as: \emph{agreement between two analyses is evidence only in
   491	proportion to the depth of the primitives they do not share}---minimizer,
   492	table, column, response model, prior document. $N$ agents reading the same
   493	inputs are one opinion wearing $N$ hats.
   494	
   495	\subsection{The four-channel experiment: generators, not adjudicators}
   496	
   497	We tested whether a panel of AI reviewers could adjudicate a genuinely
   498	contested scientific question---a burst for which two published analyses of
   499	nearly the same data disagree about a thermal component. Four reviewer
   500	channels examined disjoint evidence primitives: the spectral-panel
   501	\emph{images} only; the numeric \emph{fit tables} only; the block-to-block
   502	\emph{evolution tracks} only; and an \emph{adversary} with full access,
   503	briefed to refute the component honestly and permitted to run its own
   504	diagnostic refits. A separately-briefed adjudicator then audited all four.
   505	
   506	The outcome was double-edged. As \emph{generators}, the channels were
   507	excellent: the image channel found a figure-construction defect invisible in
   508	any table; the adversary localized a cross-normalization anomaly that we
   509	later identified---via the published literature---as a physically occulted
   510	detector, and demoted a ``decisive'' margin to an artifact of a railed
   511	reference model, both findings surviving audit and entering the engine as
   512	permanent stamps. As \emph{adjudicators}, the channels failed exactly as the
   513	doctrine predicts: the two numeric channels derived identical margin ladders
   514	and returned opposite verdicts (the disagreement was doctrinal, not
   515	evidential); the panel's one unanimous conclusion was traceable verbatim to
   516	a rule in the shared Skill Library---prescribed unanimity, not measurement;
   517	and one channel confabulated statistics that do not appear in its own
   518	assigned figure, caught only because the adjudicator reopened the figure.
   519	Two corollaries entered the doctrine. First, \emph{verify the adversary
   520	too}: the adversary claimed a nondeterministic fitting step; five identical
   521	reruns showed spread exactly zero\prov---its variance had been its own
   522	varying invocations. Second, with/without-data refits are attribution
   523	diagnostics only; a data-dropped fit is never evidence for a claim
   524	(\S\ref{sec:doctrine}).
   525

   530	independent Stage-1 selections from experienced researchers, and agents from

notes/literature_tier1/bn130427324.md:64:GRB 130427A is one of the most heavily studied GBM bursts and touches nearly all of our questions: blackbody/photosphere (Preece's 4-sigma BB in the onset pulse; Ruffini-group Band+BB SN-rise with kT~28.7 keV; Du+2022 thermal-in-main-burst; late 0.5->0.1 keV BB), Ep evolution and synchrotron-vs-curvature in a single bright pulse (Preece), a second/extra hard component and high-energy behavior (Ackermann, Tam, Fan — though largely afterglow-phase), and low-energy indices vs the synchrotron death line (Du+2022).
